scope: Proposition 7.1 (A cycle of common exclusion continua) of the manuscript “The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable” (preprints/The-Euclidean-plane-is-not-five-colorable-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 158 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 607c2601b5ae655c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 42-43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the weak measurable five-coloring under consideration, there exist an integer ℓ ∈ {3, 4, 5}, distinct labels i0, . . . , iℓ−1 ∈ I, a point x ∈ R2, and a radius ρ > 0 with the following properties. For each edge ijij+1 of the simple label cycle, with indices modulo ℓ, there are a compact connected set Kj ⊂ B(x, ρ), a direction vj ∈ S, and a sequence qj,k ∈ Kj \ {x} such that 1. x ∈ Kj and Kj ∩ ∂B(x, ρ) ̸= ∅; 2. qj,k → x and (qj,k − x)/|qj,k − x| → vj; 42 3. both endpoint supports are excluded from the same open set: Hij ∩ ∆(Kj) = Hij+1 ∩ ∆(Kj) = ∅. The extracted cycle need not consist of edges of Γx.
